newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-GRAF ENDS NOVOTNA STREAK, TO MEET HINGIS IN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF ENDS NOVOTNA STREAK, TO MEET HINGIS IN FINAL.

text.p: Steffi Graf stopped the brilliant run of Jana Novotna with a come-from-behind, three-set win to set up a showdown with up-and-comer Martina Hingis in Sunday's final of the Chase Championships.

Graf lost the first set and was down a break in the third of the brilliant battle but raised her game -- and benefitted from a Novotna lapse -- to snap the Czech's 14-match win streak 4-6 6-4 6-3 in Saturday's semifinals of the season-ending event.
"It was pretty difficult," world number one Graf admitted after the two-hour struggle.
"I thought it was a really spectacular match," the 28-year-old Novotna said. "I gave everything that I had. She was just better at the end. She's just a great champion."
The 16-year-old Hingis also went three sets but had a far easier time defeating friend and former doubles partner Iva Majoli of Croatia 6-2 4-6 6-1.

Graf leads her personal series against Hingis 4-1, losing last May to the rising star in the quarters of the Italian Open and most recently beating her in the fourth round at Wimbledon and in the semifinals of the U.S. Open.
The final brings a $500,000 prize to the winner.
"She's been playing some really, really good tennis the last few months," Graf said about the fifth-ranked Hingis.
"She's obviously one of the up and coming players. She's got a fresh attitude, she goes out there and enjoys herself and just hits out. It's obviously going to be exciting."
Graf improved her career mark against Novotna to 26-4 but the Czech looked at least her equal until breaking down towards the end of a match that saw some spectacular shot-making.

With the climactic set on serve in the sixth game Novotna had a mental lapse, letting a floating backhand service return drop in without making a play to set up break point. She then double-faulted to give Graf a 4-2 lead.
That was all the top-seeded German needed, as she roared on to claim victory in the best match of the 16-player event.
"She really showed she has the capability," said Graf, who quit in the final against Novotna last Sunday in Philadelphia because of back spasms.
"She doesn't make a lot of mistakes any more. There are no easy errors. You have to play well to beat her."

Novotna's slip in the sixth game recalled her third-set collapse in the 1993 Wimbledon final against Graf, where she double-faulted when she was one point away from taking a 5-1 lead and then never won another game.
But the Czech would not ruminate over her mistakes, instead taking comfort from the sensational form she exhibited.
"I couldn't be happier with the way I've been playing," said the third-ranked Novotna, who won 101 total points in the match to 100 for Graf. "In the end she was just a better player than I was."
Novotna played the semifinal in a celebratory mood, diving recklessly for volleys, applauding great Graf shots and flopping down theatrically at the end of an exhausting point.
Graf, 27, maintained a dead-pan cool, calling upon a refuse-to-lose champion's grit when it appeared the match might be getting away.
The German did not rate the contest as highly as Novotna and was relieved to escape with victory.

"She had her chances, but at the end whenever it got to important points maybe I was playing a little better," said Graf. "I was happy to be able to pull that match out. I don't think I'm at the height of my game."
Graf traced problems with her serve and her service returns to rustiness. Since winning the U.S. Open in September, she has played just six tournament matches.
Novotna, however, had a lot to do with putting Graf on the defensive as she sparkled from the service line, at the net and off her groundstrokes.
The fifth seed won the first set on a single service break in the fifth game. Graf broke Novotna in the last game of the second set to level the match after losing her serve in the previous game.
The Czech bounced back to open the third set with a service break, which Graf nullified with a break in the fourth game before taking advantage of Novotna's costly lapse two games later.

The defeat ended Novotna's hopes of finishing the season with four successive titles. The Czech, winner of three events in the last five weeks, could have moved up to a career best number two ranking if she had beaten Graf.
